POLITICAL TRANSITIONS ATLAS — S010 EXECUTION PROMPT
Requested by Hugh Lamarque on 13 November 2026.

Update the existing Political Transitions Atlas to open with mechanism colouring. Preserve the Border Closure Atlas design model, all functioning filters and exports, the existing Site identity and its audience. Explicit URL choices may override the default; Reset must restore mechanism.

Research every country still marked partial in S009 across the entire fixed event window, 11 November 2016–11 November 2026 inclusive. Start from its office-chain ledger, unresolved questions, source records and prior review. For every relevant office or governing authority establish the opening holder, every intervening substantive change or interruption, and the endpoint. Resolve all outstanding scope, caretaker/vacancy, parallel-authority, collective-membership, double-counting and operative-date questions. Search official instruments, government/parliamentary chronologies and reliable contemporary reporting, including original-language sources. Open and read the material supporting each determination. Search snippets, current holder pages alone, and absence of search results do not prove a complete sequence.

Use the established counting protocol. Keep personal/authority handovers and collective-composition changes separate. Preserve stable IDs, date ranges, uncertain holder identities, evidence provenance and sensitivity alternatives. Do not manufacture full coverage by changing definitions, excluding difficult cases without evidence, merging incompatible units, backfilling exact dates, or treating legal reappointment as a new substantive handover. A body may be out of scope only with an explicit sourced assessment of its powers and actual role. A range may be compatible with full coverage only if it does not conceal uncertainty about the number, identity or continuity of authorities.

For each of the 36 partial countries, produce an explicit disposition for every open question: resolved with a documented finding, or unresolved with the exact missing evidence and a concrete reopening condition. Aim to close every partial, but upgrade an office or country to full_window_verified only when the substantive gate passes. Distinguish a completed research pass from verified full-period coverage. Do not guarantee an evidence result in advance.

Sense-check the whole register and website. Check chronology, successors/predecessors, duplicate events and linked episodes, scope and mechanisms, date precision, count reconciliation, source support, contemporary plausibility, map joins and aggregate denominators. Challenge surprising or weakly supported late-window records using sources actually opened, and expand the audit if that reveals a systematic problem. Correct or hold unsupported claims transparently. Have another agent review every proposed new/changed core factual claim and country upgrade by opening the cited source material, recording disagreements and common-source dependence. This is separate-agent verification, not human validation or a statistical completeness estimate.

Integrate approved corrections and additions into a new checkpoint, preserving S009 as the prior baseline. Recompute all counts and coverage summaries from records. Regenerate the workbook, methodology/findings report, working dataset package and website exports. Keep public explanatory text readable and exact about coverage. Validate data consistency and inspect the website at desktop and phone sizes, including default/Reset state, country details, filters and downloads. Redeploy the existing Site with its current access policy. Save the prompt, research/review decisions, source trail and verification results alongside the deliverables. Report what actually changed, full-period coverage achieved and any evidence limitations that remain.
